prs.title: feat(nuxt,vite-server): render the error page in the renderer itself
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

### 📚 Description

currently, we perform a second render when there's an issue rendering. we encode the error in a query, and make a _fresh request_ to `/__nuxt_error` with this query, then render that error fresh.

this is one of the more idiosyncratic behaviours, although it did allow for clearly isolating error context

@pi0 has been suggesting for a while that it's a good idea for us to consider a simple try/catch around the renderer, and I agree....

this PR moves the error render into `fetch`; on the same event:

- the caught error is normalised, handed to `captureError` and `onDevError`, and we then render `error.vue` is with a fresh `NuxtSSRContext`
- we keep the headers and cookies the failed render had already written (for free, because it's the same event)
- we avoid having to track recursion as it's a simple try/catch
- JSON requests _do_ throw and avoid the `error.vue` entirely

because this is a bigger change, it's gated behind `experimental.inlineErrorRendering`, which is enabled by default from `compatibilityVersion: 5`.

### 🚨 Bigger changes

this is intended to be non-breaking, but it's worth pointing out that:

- error renders don't go through Nitro middleware or route rules a second time
- `render:html` fires for the error page with the _original_ event, and `x-nitro-prerender` hints are also collected from the original event
- modules listening on Nitro's `error` hook still fire, through `captureError`
- `/__nuxt_error` is no longer

prs.title: fix(nuxt): reuse pending transition promise in layout `onBeforeLeave`
prs.author: mgschwend
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

resolves #36394

### 📚 Description

When a navigation switches layout and the incoming page's suspense goes pending, `NuxtPage`'s `onPending` creates `nuxtApp['~transitionPromise']`. The leaving page's head entries defer their `dispose()` onto that promise (#35016). Then `NuxtLayout`'s `onBeforeLeave` replaces the promise with a new one, and `onAfterLeave` resolves only the new one, so the first promise never settles and the leaving page's head entries are never removed (stale title and meta, and the entry list grows per navigation).

This makes `onBeforeLeave` reuse a pending promise (`||=`), mirroring the guard in `NuxtPage`'s `onPending`. `onAfterLeave` then resolves that promise, still at the end of the layout leave, so the scroll timing from #34206 is unchanged (its cross-layout test still passes).

Added a runtime test in `test/nuxt/nuxt-layout.test.ts`: switch layout from a page that sets a title to a page with async setup, and assert that the old title's entry is removed. It fails without the change.

Ran `pnpm test:runtime` (946 passed), `pnpm typecheck` and eslint on the changed files.

prs.title: fix(kit): resolve symlinked layer directories to their real path
prs.author: silverbackdan
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

Resolves #36401

### 📚 Description

The `build:manifest` hook in `packages/nuxt/src/pages/module.ts` filters page chunks out of the entry chunk's `dynamicImports` by comparing `relative(srcDir, page.file)` against the Vite manifest keys. Vite resolves symlinks when it builds those keys, so a page in a layer reached through a symlink never matches, and is prefetched on every route.

Both sides of the comparison are now resolved through `realpath`, not just `page.file`. That distinction matters, because **which** side carries the symlink depends on `resolve.preserveSymlinks`:

| `resolve.preserveSymlinks` | Vite manifest key | `relative(srcDir, page.file)` | today |
|---|---|---|---|
| `false` (default) | real path | symlink path | they differ — **the bug** |
| `true` | symlink path | symlink path | they agree — **works** |

So resolving only `page.file` would fix the default case and break the `preserveSymlinks: true` one, which works today. Resolving both is what makes the comparison independent of the setting. I checked both against the reproduction, before and after.

(That also makes `vite: { resolve: { preserveSymlinks: true } }` a workaround on current versions, for anyone who finds this before it's released.)

A path that can't be resolved falls back to itself, so virtual ids in `dynamicImports` — which `join(srcDir, id)` can't turn into a real file — are treated exactly as they are now.

The same hook's server-only-page comparison has the same sha

prs.title: fix(kit): do not warn when updateRuntimeConfig runs before nitro exists
prs.author: Neekoras
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

Fixes #36396

### 📚 Description

`updateRuntimeConfig()` called from a module's `setup()` prints this on every `nuxt dev` and `nuxt build` since 4.5:

```
WARN  [NUXT_B8003] Nitro is not initialized yet: useNitro() was called before the ready hook ran.
```

The config is still applied, so the warning is noise, and it names an API the module author never called.

`updateRuntimeConfig` merges into `nuxt.options.nitro.runtimeConfig` and then calls `useNitro().updateConfig()` inside a `try`/`catch`, since Nitro does not exist yet during module setup. After the diagnostics rework, building `NUXT_B8003` reports it through its console reporter, so the warning is printed as the error is constructed and the `catch` cannot suppress it.

This calls `tryUseNitro()?.updateConfig()` instead, which is the documented helper for exactly this case, so no diagnostic is constructed. It also covers the other case `tryUseNitro` documents, a `server.builder` that is not backed by Nitro, where the old code was relying on a throw for normal control flow. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged: the merge above is what Nitro reads when it is created.

Verified in `playground` with the module from the issue: before, `nuxt build` prints the warning once; after, the build output has no `NUXT_B8003`.

Tests in `packages/kit/test/runtime-config.test.ts` cover the three cases: the merge, `updateConfig` being called when there is a Nitro instance, and no `console.warn` when there is not. The l
…(truncated)

prs.author: saini-25
prs.body:
Resolves #36405

Browser notices (like the ResizeObserver loop limit) emit an ErrorEvent with `event.error === null`. Adding a null check in `dev-error-overlay.client.ts` stops them from opening the full-screen error overlay.

Included an automated Playwright test in `test/e2e/dev-error-client.test.ts`.

prs.title: feat(nuxt): serve unmatched public asset paths on client-side navigation
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

### 📚 Description

sometimes users link to public files. they 'should' use the `external` attribute to opt out of client-side routing, but sometimes this isn't intuitive or workable (e.g. [with nuxt/content in markdown](https://github.com/nuxt/content/issues/3831))

the best behaviour would be for this to be detected _statically_ and an `<a>` link to be rendered (watch this space!) but in the intervening time we can 'fall through' to a hard reload when vue router is unaware of any such link

~~we can use a bloom filter to reduce false positives (thanks to the great @samwho for [this amazing explainer](https://samwho.dev/bloom-filters))~~

**update: I decided to opt-out of the bloom filter for now, and enable this by default**

**key question**: I would love feedback on how we decide to do a hard-reload vs show a client-side 404 error:
1. ~~this approach (bloom filter)~~
2. ~~always making a HEAD request (find if a file exists)~~
3. just always do a hard-reload

a bloom filter is most complex but is a best effort at better user experience.

... the latter two options are simpler but means at least 1 network round-trip. (on the other hand, links to client-side 404s are rare, so potentially the simplicity is worth it?)

prs.title: fix(nuxt): refresh component imports after rename
prs.author: oritwoen
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

Fixes #31569
closes https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/34628

### 📚 Description

This is a minimal and clean alternative to the overly complicated https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/34628. The loader already contains all the data; there’s no need for timeouts or additional observations.

Adding a Set that stores the identifiers of the modules modified by the loader is sufficient for development. The problem was that renaming a component left the modules with an import of the deleted file. Now, when a component is added or removed registry is refreshed, and then the transformation of modules from object identifiers is re-executed.
